# The relation disjoint of IEEE 1788, round-up intervals

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `upward_rel_disjoint_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

A kernel of the round-up interval ([its kernels](upward.md)), of the opt-in header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`). No operation of it rounds: it gives the same result in every rounding mode.

## What it computes

Whether $X$ and $Y$ have no member in common, $X = [-x_n, x_u]$ and $Y = [-y_n, y_u]$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies X \cap Y = \emptyset.$$

A state of the round-up interval is stored as its upper bound and its lower bound negated, the two lanes of one register: $X$ as $(x_u, x_n)$, $Y$ as $(y_u, y_n)$ ([its kernels](upward.md#the-stored-pair)).

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ieee1788::disjoint(X, Y)` | `upward::Interval<T>`, `upward::Interval<T>` | `bool` | exact: does not round, the same result in every rounding mode; not `constexpr` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; `upward::Interval<T>` is the round-up interval `kairn::upward::Interval<T>`, and `Interval<T, 1>` the default `kairn::Interval<T, 1>`. The operations are in namespace `kairn::upward`, header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`); an operation that rounds runs only inside an upward scope. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X = [-x_n, x_u]$, stored as $(x_u, x_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval: the empty set, both lanes a NaN; or a nonempty interval, each lane a number of `T` or $+\infty$ (neither a NaN nor $-\infty$), with $-x_n \le x_u$; its members are the real numbers between $-x_n$ and $x_u$.
- $Y = [-y_n, y_u]$, stored as $(y_u, y_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval: the empty set, both lanes a NaN; or a nonempty interval, each lane a number of `T` or $+\infty$ (neither a NaN nor $-\infty$), with $-y_n \le y_u$; its members are the real numbers between $-y_n$ and $y_u$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when $X$ and $Y$ have no member in common: the answer is exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, no operation of the kernel rounding, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `upward_rel_disjoint_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeUpwardPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeUpwardPredicates.v), against `upward_rel_disjoint_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/UpwardStatements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/UpwardStatements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions upward_rel_disjoint_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/UpwardAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/UpwardAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`

Which of them the proof of `upward_rel_disjoint_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the lanes compared with the negated lanes, and a test of emptiness (the listing of the round-up interval). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/upward_rel_disjoint_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/upward_rel_disjoint_1.kernel), the description the C++ (`include/kairn/gen/upward.hpp`) and the formal model (`proofs/gen/UpwardModel.v`) are generated from. Each statement is one operation of `T`, and none rounds to nearest ([the round-up interval in the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-round-up-interval)); `unord(a, b)` is whether $a$ or $b$ is a NaN.

```
# Whether two intervals of the round-up interval have no member in common (IEEE 1788 disjoint): an
# operand empty, or one above the other; the default interval_rel_disjoint_1 on the meanings. Exact,
# in every rounding mode (docs/developer/design/upward.md, "Predicates and comparisons"). Requires
# the rounding mode upward set by kairn::upward::Scope and the options of docs/concepts/upward.md
# (GCC and Clang -frounding-math, MSVC /fp:strict).

ee = unord(xu, yu)
nx = neg(xn)
ny = neg(yn)
da = lt(xu, ny)
db = lt(yu, nx)
dd = or(da, db)
m = or(ee, dd)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- What the compiled code gives where its environment is not the one of the statement: no flush to zero of results or operands (its result does not depend on the rounding mode). That is the program's to make so, as [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md#what-the-program-guarantees) says, and no proof covers that step ([What is not machine-checked](../concepts/correctness.md#what-is-not-machine-checked)).
